claim: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash trains its sparse attention at a sequence length of 64K, not 32k, and extends context to 1M only at 34T tokens into a 45T-token pretraining run.
stance_target: the repo's framing of 'CSA2 at 32k training context' as the operating point of the shipped model
quoted_support: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is trained from scratch on a multimodal corpus comprising 45T tokens, with sparse attention trained at a sequence length of 64K and context extended to 1M tokens at 34T tokens.

claim: CSA2 assigns each attention layer one of three static modes — Full, Reindex or Reuse — sharing main KV and indexer K across layers and reusing Top-K sparse-attention indices, so not every layer runs its own indexer.
stance_target: the repo's claim that 'at 32k the indexer is a second, smaller attention running in parallel' in every layer
quoted_support: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses CSA2, which assigns each attention layer one of three static modes — Full, Reindex, or Reuse — to share main KV and indexer K across layers and reuse Top-K sparse-attention indices.

claim: The Hierarchical Sparse Indexer bounds deeper indexer cost independently of context length by restricting later indexing layers to a candidate pool built by the first Full-mode layer — so the indexer's asymptotic cost is capped rather than growing with context.
stance_target: the repo's claim that CSA2's indexer overhead is bounded and therefore not the dominant cost at 32k
quoted_support: In the decoder, a Hierarchical Sparse Indexer further restricts later indexing layers to a candidate pool constructed by the first Full Mode layer, bounding deeper indexer cost independently of context length.

claim: FP4 main KV caching (E2M1 with one E4M3 scale per 16 channels) plus the mode-sharing design brings the global KV footprint to 890 bytes per token, roughly 1/4 of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and ~437x below V4/V1.
stance_target: the claim that CSA2's payoff is mostly inference-side KV-cache compression
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash vs DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V1; global KV cache bytes per token
quoted_support: Combined with FP4 main KV caching (E2M1 format, one E4M3 scale per 16 channels), these designs reduce the global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token — roughly 1/4 of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

claim: Engram conditional memory is a 196B-parameter block inside the 552B-backbone model, sparsely accessed via token-based lookup — i.e. frozen/conditional memory can be a large fraction of total parameters rather than a rounding error.
stance_target: the repo's Memory Grafting claim that a 7B-total model can be mostly frozen Engram tables with only ~1B trainable
quoted_support: Additional architectural components include Single-Pass mHC (revised residual-stream mixing with an efficient Mega-mHC kernel), Engram conditional memory (196B parameters, sparsely accessed via token-based lookup), and DSpark speculative decoding.

claim: The MoE shape is 1 shared expert plus 384 routed experts per layer with 6 routed experts active per token, and the CED split activates only 8B params/token in prefill and 16B in decode out of 552B total.
stance_target: what sparsity ratio a 1B-scale MoE experiment on this box should imitate
quoted_support: The model uses 1 shared expert and 384 routed experts per MoE layer, activating 6 routed experts per token. ... This allows the model to activate only 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decode.

claim: SWA Bounded Replay reconstructs missing sliding-window KV by replaying only the most recent n_win tokens instead of persisting SWA KV to SSD, cutting the persistent KV footprint to roughly 1/8 of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
stance_target: whether long-context serving on a memory-constrained box can avoid offloading KV to host/SSD
quoted_support: SWA Bounded Replay reconstructs missing SWA KV states by replaying only the most recent n_win tokens, avoiding the need to persist SWA KV to SSD and reducing the persistent KV cache footprint to roughly 1/8 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

claim: The model card is MIT-licensed and ships an inference reference implementation plus a Rust prompt-encoding toolkit, but gives no training throughput, no indexer FLOP accounting and no per-layer mode census — the quantitative CSA2 detail lives in the arXiv report (2609.19969), not here.
stance_target: the boundary of what the model card can be cited for
quoted_support: This repository and the model weights are licensed under the MIT License. ... Please refer to the inference folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally.
